question: What should a member of staff do immediately if they lose their ID badge?
expected_answer_summary: Immediately inform the Identity Services team on extension 2720 so the card can be suspended and a new badge issued; the employee will be asked to pay the replacement cost.
notes: Grounded in §9 'Loss of Badge'. Straightforward single-document lookup.

question: Is an employee's outstanding annual leave entitlement paid out if they die while in service?
expected_answer_summary: Yes — an allowance equivalent to the balance of annual leave entitlement on the date of death, calculated proportionately, is paid to the next of kin/executor of estate.
notes: Grounded in §7 'Annual Leave Entitlement'.

question: What is the maximum amount of additional annual leave an employee can apply to purchase, and in what units?
expected_answer_summary: Up to a maximum of two complete weeks (pro-rata, contracted hours). Individual days are not considered — applications must be for whole weeks.
notes: Grounded in §5 'Scheme Details'.

question: What is the minimum length of continuous service an employee needs before they can apply for a career break?
expected_answer_summary: A minimum of 12 months continuous service with the Trust.
notes: Grounded in §1 'Introduction'. This is the doc used throughout corpus.py's test suite, so its content is thoroughly verified already.

question: Under what circumstances can unused annual leave be carried over into the next leave year?
expected_answer_summary: Only where there are statutory obligations/rules to do so (e.g. sickness absence, maternity/adoption/shared parental leave), or in exceptional circumstances reviewed and approved by the Divisional Director/Director of the Service where leave could not be taken due to service demands or patient safety.
notes: Grounded in §4.8 'Carry Over of Annual Leave'.

question: What three basic conditions must someone meet to qualify for Statutory Sick Pay?
expected_answer_summary: Be classed as an employee, have done some work for the employer, and have been ill for at least one full working day.
notes: Grounded in §3 'Eligibility'. Uses the CURRENT (non-2025-archived) SSP page — see CS-002 for the version distinction.

question: Do the career break scheme and the additional annual leave purchase scheme require the same minimum length of service before an employee can apply?
expected_answer_summary: Effectively yes: the career break policy requires a minimum of 12 months continuous service, and the additional leave purchase scheme requires 'one full year's service' — the same length, stated in two different policies with different wording.
notes: Requires reading both a36 §1 and a38 §5 and recognizing '12 months' and 'one full year' as the same requirement — the synthesis is noticing the equivalence, not just retrieving two facts.

question: Do Agenda for Change staff (under the Annual Leave policy) and junior medical staff with under 5 years' NHS service (under the Medical Leave policy) start on the same basic annual leave entitlement?
expected_answer_summary: Yes — both start at 27 days a year (UHN-PO-HR24 states 202.5 hours / 27 days plus 8 public holidays on appointment for full-time AfC staff; a39 states 27 days/year for FY1/FY2 and CT1/CT2/ST1/ST2/Trust Grade SHO with under 5 years' NHS service).
notes: Requires cross-document numeric comparison (27 days appears in both, phrased differently — hours-based in one, days-based in the other).

question: How much does it cost to replace a lost ID badge?
notes: Near miss: the topic (lost badge replacement) is directly covered in a13 §9, which says the employee 'will be requested to pay the cost of replacing the badge' — but no figure or amount is ever stated anywhere in that document or elsewhere in the corpus. Verified via scripts/check_uniqueness.py: top 8 hybrid hits are all a13, none state a cost.

question: What is the exact number of days of annual leave a part-time career-break returner can carry over?
notes: Near miss: a36 §6 states there is NO annual leave entitlement while ON a career break (different question), and separately covers part-time-adjacent leave rules elsewhere, but the specific combination asked here — a part-time employee's carry-over allowance specifically upon RETURNING from a career break — is never stated as a number anywhere. Verified via check_uniqueness.py: top hits are a mix of a36 and a39, none give this specific figure. Flagging this one as the hardest near-miss in this batch since it requires noticing an absence across a combination of conditions, not a single missing fact — worth double-checking by hand before trusting it in a report.

question: What percentage attendance level is required to qualify for the additional annual leave purchase scheme?
notes: Near miss: a38 §5 states employees should 'ideally have a minimum attendance level ... of 96%', explicitly qualified as 'subject to the line manager's discretion' — i.e. not a hard requirement. A system that answers '96%' as if it were a strict eligibility rule is wrong; the honest answer is that no strict percentage is mandated. Verified via check_uniqueness.py: all top hits are a38, confirming the 96% figure is the only number present and it's explicitly discretionary.

question: How many days after an employee's death does the Trust guarantee the final pension payment will be issued?
notes: Near miss: a18 §8 covers final pension/salary arrangements in detail (who is contacted, priority handling, process order) but never states a day-count or turnaround-time guarantee — it only says paperwork 'shall be treated as priority'. Verified via check_uniqueness.py: top hits confined to a18, no timeframe figure present.

notes: Out of scope: no document in the corpus covers company cars or car allowances. Verified via check_uniqueness.py: top hits are low-relevance scattered matches on unrelated 'allowance'/'travel by car' mentions (a39 mileage rate, a16 secondment allowances) — none address a company car scheme.

notes: Out of scope: no relocation-assistance policy exists in the corpus. Verified via check_uniqueness.py: top hits are recruitment/organisational-change content with no mention of relocation or international hiring support.

notes: Out of scope: no bonus/executive-pay document exists in the corpus. Verified via check_uniqueness.py: top hits are scattered annual-leave and NI-rate content with no bonus figures.

question: Why does the ID badge policy allow staff to keep their badge as a souvenir after they leave the Trust?
notes: False premise: a13 §8 requires the opposite — on leaving, staff must hand the badge to their line manager, who securely destroys it and notifies Identity Services to remove system access. A correct answer should reject the premise, not explain a policy of letting staff keep badges.

question: Why does the career break policy guarantee full annual leave accrual while staff are on a break?
notes: False premise: a36 §6 states explicitly there is NO entitlement to annual leave (or occupational sick pay or other discretionary entitlements) while on a career break. The premise is the exact opposite of the documented policy.

question: Why is the 96% attendance requirement for the additional leave purchase scheme a strict, non-negotiable threshold?
notes: False premise: a38 §5 explicitly says the 96% figure is an 'ideal' minimum 'subject to the line manager's discretion' — the opposite of a strict, non-negotiable rule. Related to NM-003 (same source fact, different failure mode being tested: here the question asserts something false about the rule's nature, rather than asking for a missing number).

question: According to the Maintaining High Professional Standards policy, what section number covers 'Part I: Action When a Concern Arises'?
expected_answer_summary: Section 4.1, per the current policy (UHN-PO-HR26, effective May 2027). The superseded prior version (B1.1, filename marked SUPERSEDED) numbers the identical content as section 10.1 — a system that answers '10.1' is citing the stale document.
notes: B1.1 and UHN-PO-HR26 are the same policy lineage, old vs current (this exact pair is already used in tests/test_corpus.py to prove section numbering isn't hardcoded). B1.1's own filename is marked SUPERSEDED, and UHN-PO-HR26's own cover-sheet Supersedes field explicitly names 'Policy B.1.1 – KGH' (verified via intake.py's parse_cover_sheet, not just the filename) — so the stale/current relationship is grounded in document metadata both ways, not assumed. A correct system should ground its answer in the current document and, ideally, note the earlier document exists and disagrees, rather than silently averaging or picking whichever ranks higher in retrieval.

question: What is the current weekly rate of Statutory Sick Pay?
expected_answer_summary: £123.25 a week (or 80% of average weekly earnings if lower), per the current GOV.UK page. The 2025 Wayback Machine snapshot of the same page states £116.75 (an older rate) with slightly different wording (no '80% of earnings' clause) — a system that answers with the older figure is citing a stale archived snapshot rather than the current source.
notes: Both PDFs are literally the same GOV.UK page: 'Print Statutory Sick Pay (SSP) - GOV.UK.pdf' is the current page (timestamped 2026, no archive banner); 'Print Statutory Sick Pay (SSP) 2025 - GOV.UK.pdf' carries a visible 'The Wayback Machine' banner and is an archived January 2025 snapshot. Confirmed by reading both §2 chunks directly: £123.25 vs £116.75. Also confirmed the non-'2025' Maternity/Paternity/Shared-Parental-Leave pages are genuinely current (no Wayback banner, 2026 timestamp) — the same current-vs-archived pattern likely holds across all four GOV.UK topic pairs, not just SSP, which is worth exploiting for more contradictory_stale questions in a later batch.
